notes: HIS FIRST RULING was one word, on a question with two parts. Asked whether the fives recal_206's play-volume gate knocked out of helio should have ISO as their home: "1) Yes." And asked what the Spurs '16 are instead: "2) Motion, or balanced."

HIS SECOND RULING sent the first cut back: "You have moved post up players into iso. AD, Bosh, Embid, are all post players not iso." He was right and it was systematic. ISO_JMP reads max(mid, 3pt), and a back-to-the-basket big has an enormous MID-RANGE - Embiid '23 mid 98, Davis '16 92, Bosh '10 88 - so he was nominated as a jump-shooting iso man; and isoRoom then charged him almost nothing for spacing because his three is low. That is the wrong half of two rules at once, and it is why those three outbid their own post-up.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS HEIGHT, AND IT WAS ALREADY IN THE FILE. Measured against his own two groups: he KEPT Dantley '81 h77, DeRozan '17 h78, Leonard '16 h78, King '84 h79, Gervin '82 h79, Anthony '13 h79, Vandeweghe '84 h80; he THREW OUT Davis '16 h82, Bosh '10 h83, Embiid '23 h84. Nothing else parts them - rim does not (Dantley 99 and King 98 are higher than all three exclusions), mid does not (Embiid 98 sits above Leonard 92), the three does not (Dantley 12 and Bosh 15 are neighbours), volume does not. The line between 80 and 82 is POST_HEIGHT 81, which postMan already uses for the mirror-image job, and which is itself measured: the men postMan nominates run p10 81, p50 82.

SO THE TWO NOMINATIONS PARTITION THE FLOOR at the line that was already there. postMan only ever nominates a man POST_HEIGHT or taller; isoMan only ever nominates a man the post-up would not take. No new threshold: facesUp reads BOTH of postMan's facts - under POST_HEIGHT, or that tall and playing outside, which is postFit's own interior() scaling.

IT READS BOTH FACTS AND NOT HEIGHT ALONE BECAUSE OF DURANT. A bare height < POST_HEIGHT gate was measured first: it satisfies his ruling and lands 45 of 1,255, but it also deletes Durant '23 (h83), whose Nets nominate Irving instead and fall out of iso at 57.0 - contradicting the half of his first ruling that this style exists for. Durant shoots 78 from three, Nowitzki '12 63, so postFit gives them exactly 0 and the post-up was never going to have them. Reading both facts lands 55 and keeps them.

AND IT IS A GATE ON THE NOMINATION, NOT A TERM IN THE PRICE - recal_124's doctrine verbatim: "Height decides who the ENGINE will nominate, not what a man the CALLER names is worth." isoScore carries no height term, so a plan that names Embiid as its iso scorer prices Embiid, and naming him scores HIGHER than the man the gate leaves behind because he is the better one-on-one scorer. The house rule is intact: the price is continuous, only the engine's default pick is partitioned.

THE COUNT FELL, as expected: iso 81 of 1,255 (6.5%) before the fix, 55 (4.4%) after - still a signature system and not padded back up. The wheel reads balanced 470 / pnr 316 / postup 235 / helio 141 / triangle 45 / pickpop 25 / fiveout 19 / motion 4 without iso, and balanced 440 / pnr 310 / postup 232 / helio 131 / iso 55 / triangle 42 / pickpop 25 / fiveout 17 / motion 3 with it. Taken from balanced 30, helio 10, pick-and-roll 6, post-up 3, triangle 3, five-out 2, motion 1.

HIS RULING, FIVE BY FIVE. LEFT iso: Pelicans '16 -> postup 73.8 (iso 52.0), '17 -> postup 71.7 (33.3), '15 -> pnr 75.5 (40.8), '14 -> pnr 62.7 (24.3); Raptors '10 -> pnr 68.5 (51.4), '08 -> pnr 74.8 (35.6), '06 -> pnr 70.4 (45.9), '09 -> pnr 66.3 (1.8); 76ers '22 -> helio 68.8 (50.4), '24 -> helio 63.0 (58.7), '21 -> balanced 60.0 (48.6), '18 -> postup 66.2 (46.6), '19 -> postup 60.8 (36.1). STAYED iso, all 26 of them: DeRozan (Raptors '17, Spurs '20, Bulls '22/'23, Kings '26), Leonard (Spurs '17, Raptors '19, Clippers '21/'23), Anthony (Knicks '13/'16), Dantley (Jazz '80/'81/'82/'84/'85/'86, Pistons '87/'88/'89), King (Knicks '83/'84), Durant (Nets '23), Vandeweghe (Nuggets '83/'84, Blazers '85/'86), Gervin (Spurs '80/'81/'82/'83), Maggette (Clippers '05, Warriors '09).

ISO_PV FOLLOWED ITS OWN DEFINITION. The constant is the median play volume of the man the fit nominates; the gate changed which man that is, so the measurement moved 53 -> 57 and the constant went with it rather than being held where it was first taken. ISO_PV_W is now HELIO_PV_W's own 0.45 - one line, two sides, the same price per point either way - because the gate destroyed the only evidence for 0.55 (it had been kept to widen the Jazz '97 anchor from 3.1 to 4.2, and that anchor now clears by 36.9). 0.55 was re-measured and lands 53 fives instead of 55, moving no ruling and no anchor.

THE SPURS '16 STILL DO NOT COME, by his ruling on them ("2) Motion, or balanced."): balanced 60.0, iso 54.0, six points of margin on the shipped cards. Thunder '15 is still pnr 71.4 (iso 42.0). recal_206's helio head is unmoved: Lakers '87 67.0, Nuggets '22 76.8, Cavaliers '18 73.1, Mavericks '24 64.9, Rockets '15 74.7, Heat '09 69.4, Warriors '16 69.3, 76ers '06 64.7.

EVERY STYLE ANCHOR HOLDS, and the gate widened every one of them. Thinnest margin first: Celtics '25 fiveout 72.8 to iso 66.3 (6.5), Thunder '25 pnr 74.2 / 63.6 (10.6), Thunder '22 helio 65.3 / 54.1 (11.2), Bulls '96 triangle 72.8 / 63.3 (9.5), Bulls '97 75.0 / 61.0 (14.0), Magic '11 postup 81.6 / 54.5 (27.1), Jazz '97 pnr 76.2 / 39.3 (36.9), Rockets '18 pnr 90.8 / 55.7 (35.1), Hornets '95 postup 77.7 / 35.3 (42.4), Suns '05 pnr 84.9 / 29.5 (55.4), Nuggets '25 pnr 72.9 / 51.1 (21.8).

THE ONE KNOB THAT NEEDED MEASURING, and it survives the fix unchanged: the spacing price. A flat charge per non-shooter cannot be right at both ends of the league's history - at 8 a point it read the Spurs '16 45.3 (correct) and the Jazz '81 33.3 and Knicks '84 31.0 (wrong), and dropping it to 3 takes iso to 165 fives and hands it the Spurs. A wing iso needs a driving lane; a mid-post iso beats his man in traffic. isoRoom is 1 - interior(), 0 at 3pt <= 20 rising continuously to 1 at 3pt >= SHOOT_3PT_HI 60. Leonard '16 pays the full 8 a man; Dantley '81 pays nothing.

THE CAMPAIGN LADDER DOES NOT REORDER. bestStyle is read in exactly two places - CourtFive (the scouting drawing and its caption) and TeamDb (a filter chip) - and by nothing in the sim or the resolver, so a style read cannot move a margin. Two of the 30 campaign opponents' DISPLAYED reads change: Kings '26 balanced 60.0 -> iso 64.5 (DeRozan) and Heat '26 five-out 69.1 -> iso 70.5 (Powell). Both survive the fix; every opponent rating and every round's position is byte-identical.

THE DEVIATION TAX LAW still passes with nine styles in the pool: playstyle reads default 0.00, random -1.37, oracle +2.03 against its band of oracle >= +0.50 and random in [-1.50, -0.30]. No tax constant was touched.

NO CARD MOVED AND NO RATING MOVED. src/engine/offense.ts and data/team_rating.py are untouched, so nothing in the OVR chain, nothing in marg, and nothing in the anchor table can have moved. 212 anchors, 0 failing, mean |error| 1.00 - the same table main shipped.
cost: STYLES is nine long now and iso is appended, so no existing key changed index; two tests that asserted toHaveLength(8) now assert 9 (tests/tactics.test.ts).

Tactics gains a fourth name-keyed one-man call, `iso`, on the same three rules as post/helio: reconcileTactics drops it when the man leaves the five, gateTactics silences it below Playbook 2, and absent/null means the engine's own scorer.

facesUp is the THIRD reader of POST_HEIGHT and the third of interior(): a round that re-cuts either moves the post-up hub, the iso spacing price and the iso nomination together, and postMan/isoMan will stay complementary only if both keep reading the same constant.

THE COST OF THE GATE, recorded rather than hidden: on a five whose only real scorer is a post big, the engine's default iso man is now the best face-up scorer left, and that can be a minor one - Ryan Anderson for the Pelicans '16, Redick for the 76ers '18, Byron Scott for the Lakers '87 (whose Johnson '87 is exactly h81 and interior, so the gate excludes him). None of those reaches a caption on its own: every one of those fives reads another style by 13 to 39 points, and a plan that wants the big named says so.

Those two want his word.
